title: data-labeling-cleanup-notes
content:
Context: personal scratchpad for the data labeling cleanup pass (embedding and supervised datasets). Mostly notes + examples I want to use when we brief the labelers next week.

Goals:
- reduce label noise in the chat-intent and toxic-content datasets
- create deterministic heuristics for ambiguous cases so cross-labeler variance is low
- document edge cases for escalations to an adjudication queue

Quick summary of proposed labels (short names we use in pipeline):
- intent: request | info | feedback | other
- toxicity: toxic | non-toxic | borderline
- personal_data: pii | non-pii | ambiguous-pii
- quality: ok | spam | gibberish | empty
- instruction_following: follows | partial | ignores

Heuristics / rules (working):
1) "request" vs "info": any utterance explicitly asking for an action ("Can you...", "Please generate...", specific ask for code/snippet/data) -> request. Otherwise factual questions or explanatory statements -> info. If the user expresses sentiment about the product -> feedback.
2) Toxicity borderline heuristics: if profanity appears but in a reclaimed / quote context (e.g., "they said 'f**k' in the logs") mark borderline + add comment. If slur directed at a protected class -> toxic. If profanity used self-referentially ("I'm so f***ing tired") -> borderline unless threat/harassment is explicit.
3) PII detection: treat anything that looks like a full name + company + contact as pii if it's intended to identify a private individual. Public figure names are non-pii by default but flag if accompanied by personal contact info. 
4) Spam / gibberish: repeated characters, extremely short repeated token sequences, or random character noise -> spam/gibberish. If the message is just a URL with no other text -> spam (unless context indicates link sharing is the task).

Edge cases and sample annotations (use these as examples in the labeler guide):
- "How do I reset my password?" -> intent: request, instruction_following: follows (clear ask).
- "FYI the deployment failed at 14:03 due to OOM" -> intent: info, quality: ok.
- "You are an idiot" -> toxicity: toxic (direct insult).
- "They said \"screw this\" in the logs" -> toxicity: borderline (quoted profanity).
- "Contact John at john@example.com to fix" -> personal_data: pii (email).
- "12345-6789" (isolated numeric string) -> quality: ambiguous -> put in adjudication queue unless pattern matches known IDs we accept.
- "??!!??" or long random characters -> quality: gibberish.

Annotation examples for model training (label format: label|rationale):
- "Can you summarize this article?" -> request|explicit ask for action
- "the product was slow yesterday" -> feedback|user sentiment about product performance
- "I will kill the job if it keeps failing" -> toxic|threatening language -> escalate to safety review
- "Email me at jane.doe@company.com" -> pii|contains email address

Open questions / TODOs:
- How strict should we be on profanity used in creative / quote contexts? (makes big diff in borderline counts) -> propose: default borderline + add boolean "quoted_profanity" metadata for downstream filtering.
- Add explicit examples for non-English profanity and transliterated slurs. Need to coordinate with localization folks (Priya).
- Decide cutoff heuristics for "partial" instruction_following (25% tokens matching requested format?) -> experiment with thresholds.
- Build small adjudication UI that shows full context + previous labels from 3 annotators. Ticket: JIRA-ML-1289 (linked above).

Scripts / automation ideas:
- Pre-clean step to canonicalize emails/phones -> mask as <EMAIL>/<PHONE> and tag as pii automatically, then labelers only confirm.
- Regex pass to flag probable spam/gibberish so labelers can bulk mark.
- Auto-suggest label based on simple heuristics (if contains question mark + call to action words -> suggest request). But mustn't auto-apply; always show suggestion.

Labeler training checklist (for next sync):
- Walk through 10 curated examples + rationale (mix of easy/ambiguous).
- Show how to use adjudication queue.
- How to add comments / notes and escalate.
- Short quiz (15 items) to align on borderline cases.

Notes to self (fast):
- Keep the "adjudication" threshold flexible; start with 15% variance across labelers -> adjudicate.
- Check inter-annotator agreement after 2k labels -> compute Kripp alpha for major categories.
- Make a short Confluence page linking these examples + final guideline (once we converge).

Misc scraps / fragments I've been tossing here:
- Consider label "metadata:needs_context" when truncated conversational context might change label.
- For multimodal (images + text) examples, create separate guideline section.
- Slack convo notes: #ml-data: Luca: "we should mask all emails before showing to contractors" -> implement in pipeline.

References / quick links:
- JIRA-ML-1289 (adjudication UI)
- CONFLUENCE-PRD-3421 (labeling standard - draft)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/labeling-scripts/pull/57 (cleanup regexes)

Closing thought: this is messy but OK for first pass. Next step: convert into a tidy one-pager + 15 example packet for labeler onboarding.

-- Aisha
